about: CPU database: families are the fallback for a generation, models override one chip. match = regexes tested against the Windows CPU name.

families.name: Ryzen 9000 X3D (Zen 5 3D V-Cache)
families.ram: DDR5-6000 CL30 with EXPO, 2 sticks (1:1 memory controller).
families.tune: PBO + Curve Optimizer (BIOS): all-core -15, then -20/-30 if stable. Zen 5 X3D also allows normal PBO overclocking.
tips: Enable EXPO, then Curve Optimizer -15 all-core; test with CoreCycler before going further.
Keep chipset driver and BIOS current: AMD's newest AGESA improves X3D scheduling and memory.
issues: Keep SoC voltage at or below 1.3 V (BIOS default on current firmware).

src.T: Most Zen 4 and Zen 5 chips sustain -20, even -30 Curve Optimizer steps (each step about 3-5 mV).
CoreCycler tests Curve Optimizer stability one core at a time.

families.name: Ryzen 9000 (Zen 5)
families.tune: PBO + Curve Optimizer -15 to -30 (BIOS); Eco Mode for a cool, quiet chip.
tips: Curve Optimizer lowers voltage per boost step: cooler and often faster under load.
Eco Mode (BIOS or Ryzen Master) trades a little multi-core speed for much less heat.

src.T: Most Zen 4 and Zen 5 chips sustain -20 to -30 Curve Optimizer.

families.name: Ryzen 7000 X3D (Zen 4 3D V-Cache)
families.ram: DDR5-6000 CL30 with EXPO is the sweet spot; faster kits add almost nothing.
families.tune: Curve Optimizer -20 to -30 (PBO > Curve Optimizer, or MSI 'Kombo Strike'). No clock overclock on these chips.
tips: Curve Optimizer -20 to -30 lowers temperatures and holds 5.0 GHz boost longer.
Enable EXPO; going past DDR5-6000 gains about 3 FPS at best.
issues: Update the BIOS: 2023 updates capped SoC voltage at 1.3 V after reports of burned chips.

src.T: Optimal memory for the 7800X3D: 32 GB DDR5-6000 CL30 EXPO.
Curve Optimizer -20 gave 5.04 GHz; RAM 6000 -> 6200 only +3 FPS.
All boards handle -15 to -20 Curve Optimizer; some chips fail -20.

families.name: Ryzen 7000 (Zen 4)
families.tune: PBO + Curve Optimizer -15 to -30; Eco Mode 105 W for quiet systems.
tips: Zen 4 is designed to run up to 95 C under heavy load: that is normal, not a fault.
Curve Optimizer -20 typically lowers temperatures and keeps clocks higher.
issues: Update the BIOS (SoC voltage cap, memory compatibility).

src.T: Most Zen 4 chips sustain -20 to -30 Curve Optimizer.

families.name: Ryzen 5000 X3D (Zen 3 3D V-Cache)
families.tune: Curve Optimizer only: BIOS (AGESA 1.2.0.8+), MSI 'Kombo Strike', or the free PBO2 Tuner. Leave the power limits alone.
tips: Curve Optimizer -20 to -30 cuts temperatures from the high 80s to the low/mid 70s on many chips.
PBO2 Tuner settings reset at reboot: run it from a startup task if your BIOS has no Curve Optimizer.

src.T: On the 5800X3D only Curve Optimizer is worth touching; Kombo Strike = -10/-20/-30.

families.name: Ryzen 5000 (Zen 3)
families.ram: DDR4-3600 CL16 with FCLK 1800 (1:1); 2 sticks or 2 dual-rank.
families.tune: PBO + per-core Curve Optimizer (-10 to -30); test with CoreCycler.
tips: Per-core Curve Optimizer: best cores get smaller offsets (-5 to -15), the rest -20 to -30.
Keep FCLK at half the RAM speed (1800 for DDR4-3600) for the lowest latency.

src.T: Per-core Curve Optimizer guide for Ryzen 5000.
CoreCycler tests one core at a time.

families.name: Ryzen APU (G / Phoenix / Cezanne)
families.ram: Fastest RAM the board takes: DDR4-3600-4000 (5000G) or DDR5-6000+ (8000G). The graphics live on it.
families.tune: Curve Optimizer -15 to -30 on supported boards; raise UMA frame buffer for games.
tips: Dual-channel, fast RAM is the single biggest upgrade for the integrated graphics.

families.name: Ryzen 3000 (Zen 2)
families.tune: Little to gain from PBO; a manual all-core overclock costs single-core boost.
tips: Fast RAM with matched FCLK matters more than CPU tuning on Zen 2.

families.name: Ryzen 1000 / 2000 (Zen / Zen+)
families.tune: Precision Boost 2 (2000 series) already boosts well; keep stock or a mild all-core OC on 1000 series.
tips: A BIOS update often improves RAM compatibility on these older boards.

families.name: Core Ultra 200S (Arrow Lake)
families.ram: DDR5-7200 is the price/performance sweet spot; up to DDR5-8000 with 200S Boost.
families.tune: K chips on Z890: Intel 200S Boost profile in the BIOS (fabric + memory OC, keeps the warranty).
tips: Update the BIOS (0x114 microcode or newer improves gaming performance).
200S Boost: most of the gain comes from the faster memory, not the fabric clocks.

src.T: 200S Boost raised fabric and die-to-die clocks and allows DDR5-8000; about 7.5% higher 1080p gaming, mostly from memory.
Official 200S Boost profile: supported CPUs and how to enable it.

families.name: Core 13th / 14th gen (Raptor Lake)
families.ram: DDR5-6000 to 7200 (2 sticks) or DDR4-3600 CL16 (Gear 1).
families.tune: First: BIOS with microcode 0x12B or newer and the 'Intel Default Settings' profile. Optional: a small negative voltage offset / lower AC load line.
tips: Update the BIOS to microcode 0x12B or newer: it stops the voltage that degrades these chips.
Pick 'Intel Default Settings' (i9: 'Performance' profile) in the BIOS instead of unlimited board defaults.
Never raise CPU voltage on these chips.
issues: Vmin shift instability: the BIOS fix prevents it but cannot repair a chip that already crashes at stock; contact Intel if it does.

src.T: Root cause and the 0x12B microcode mitigation for 13th/14th gen desktop CPUs.
Intel confirmed 0x12B as the final mitigation, delivered via BIOS updates.

families.name: Core 12th gen (Alder Lake)
families.ram: DDR5-6000 or DDR4-3600 CL16 in Gear 1.
families.tune: K chips on Z690/Z790: mild all-core OC or power limits; non-K: keep stock, enable XMP.
tips: Keep E-cores enabled on Windows 11: Thread Director schedules games on P-cores.
On B660/B760 boards XMP works; CPU ratio overclocking needs Z-series.

families.name: Core 8th-11th gen
families.ram: DDR4-3200 to 3600 (11th gen: Gear 1 up to ~3600).
families.tune: K chips on Z boards: all-core OC or MCE; most BIOS updates lock CPU undervolting (Plundervolt fix).
tips: Enable XMP: many of these PCs run RAM at 2133-2666 by default.

families.name: Core 6th-7th gen
families.tune: K chips on Z170/Z270: classic all-core overclock.
tips: Windows 11 does not officially support these CPUs.

families.name: Other Intel CPU
families.ram: Enable XMP if the board allows it.

families.name: Other AMD CPU
families.ram: Enable EXPO/XMP/DOCP if the board allows it.

models.name: Ryzen 7 9800X3D
notes: 120 W TDP; unlike the 7800X3D it supports full PBO overclocking.

models.name: Ryzen 9 9950X3D / 9900X3D
notes: Two chiplets, one with V-Cache: keep the AMD chipset driver and Game Mode on so games use the cache cores.

models.name: Ryzen 7 7800X3D
notes: Boosts to 5.0 GHz; Curve Optimizer -20 reached 5.04 GHz (PCGH via Igor's Lab).

models.name: Ryzen 9 7900X3D / 7950X3D
notes: Keep the chipset driver and Game Bar current so games stay on the V-Cache chiplet.

models.name: Ryzen 7 5800X3D
notes: Max boost 4.55 GHz; Curve Optimizer is the only tuning that matters.

models.name: Ryzen 7 5700X3D
notes: Same tuning as the 5800X3D: Curve Optimizer -20 to -30.

models.name: Core i9-13900K/KF/KS, 14900K/KF/KS
notes: Most affected by Vmin shift: BIOS 0x12B+ and the Intel 'Performance' profile are a must.

models.name: Core i7-13700K / 14700K
notes: Update the BIOS (0x12B+) and use Intel Default Settings.

models.name: Core i5-13600K / 14600K (and KF)
notes: 6 P-cores + 8 E-cores; Intel Default Settings, 0x12B+ BIOS. A small undervolt lowers heat.

models.name: Core i5-12400 / 12400F
notes: P-cores only; locked: XMP and good airflow are the free wins.

models.name: Core Ultra 9 285K / Ultra 7 265K / Ultra 5 245K
notes: Supported by Intel 200S Boost on Z890 boards.

models.name: Ryzen 5 5600X / 5600
notes: Per-core Curve Optimizer + PBO typically adds 100-200 MHz of sustained boost.
